preamble: The shift from the voiced uvular fricative [ʁ] to the voiced pharyngeal fricative [ʕ] is best documented in Hebrew, where Proto-Semitic *ġ (reconstructed as [ɣ] or [ʁ]) merged with *ʕ. The Septuagint (3rd century BCE) still renders the old ghayin with Greek gamma, as in Gomorrha and Gaza, while Arabic keeps the uvular in Ġazzah [ˈɣazza]; by Tiberian Hebrew the merger was complete and both sounds were written and pronounced as ayin.

examples.note: The Greek gamma preserves the pre-merger uvular; Tiberian Hebrew writes and pronounces the word with ayin.
Same merger of ghayin with ayin, complete by the Tiberian period.
